title: Cap. V Obj. 3 Sol: preconsidered as to-be-faithful for reception, not as already faithful for destinating
pass_a_gloss: Whoever therefore is about to receive eternal life was preconsidered by God as about to be faithful, and that antecedently to the reception of eternal life: but he was not foreseen as existing faithful, and that antecedently to the destination of eternal life. Let us explain the matter by this likeness: If someone of good estate, having seen a wretched and needy infant, at once decrees in his mind to adopt him and gift him with an excellent inheritance, yet so that he not enter upon this inheritance before he has reached the years of puberty, and has been cultivated with good letters and manners; we may truly say that this inheritance was destinated to such a person considered as unlearned, as uncultivated, as an infant; but the same inheritance was gifted to such a person considered as cultivated, as learned, as of age, and that from the destinating purpose of the adopter.
pass_b_english: So whoever will receive eternal life was preconsidered by God as about to be faithful — antecedent to receiving eternal life — but not foreseen as already existing faithful — antecedent to destinating eternal life. Likeness: a man of good estate sees a wretched needy infant and at once decrees to adopt him and gift an excellent inheritance, yet not to enter it before puberty and cultivation in letters and manners. Truly that inheritance was destinated to him considered unlearned, uncultivated, an infant; yet the same inheritance was gifted to him considered cultivated, learned, of age — from the adopter's destinating purpose.
source_text: Quicunque igitur vitam aeternam accepturus est, a Deo fuit praeconsideratus ut fidelis futurus, idque antecedenter ad acceptionem vitae aeternae: sed non fuit praevisus ut fidelis existens, idque antecedenter ad destinationem vitae aeternae. Hoc simili rem explicemus: Si quis in re bene lauta, conspecto misero et inope infante, statim apud animum suum decernat illum adoptare et optima haereditate donare, ita tamen ut non adeat hanc haereditatem priusquam ad annos pubertatis pervenerit, ac bonis literis et moribus excultus fuerit; vere dicamus hanc haereditatem tali personae consideratae ut indoctae, ut incultae, ut infanti, fuisse destinatam; at eadem haereditas tali personae consideratae ut excultae, ut doctae, ut puberi, fuit donata, idque ex destinato proposito adoptantis.
